Small molecule structure elucidation from NMR spectra with generative and reasoning models.

This preprint introduces an AI system that automates de novo small-molecule structure elucidation from NMR spectra by pairing a generative model (ChefNMR2, an atomic flow-matching model) with a scientific reasoning agent. The approach aims to replace labor-intensive expert interpretation of NMR data with rapid, automated structure prediction, which could accelerate chemistry, pharmacology, and drug discovery workflows.

MultiTargetDB: a comprehensive database of multitarget ligands for polypharmacology research and drug discovery.

MultiTargetDB is a new database that curates multitarget ligands—small molecules that bind multiple biological targets—along with detailed biological annotations and measurement-level provenance. It integrates chemical structures, scaffolds, and drug development stages to support polypharmacology research and rational multitarget drug discovery. The resource addresses the scarcity of well-curated data for designing drugs that intentionally hit multiple targets in complex diseases.

Structure-function relationships in a square-planar Cu(ii) hybrid halometalate: experimental, DFT, molecular docking, optical, and biological studies.

Integrating Multisource Target Evidence with Machine-Learning Potency Prediction for Alzheimer's Disease Drug Discovery.

The authors built a traceable data-to-model platform that integrates Alzheimer's disease target evidence from biological, chemical, structural, regulatory, and trial-registry sources, covering 967 targets, 452,249 compounds, and 1,430,260 measurements. On a curated PIK3CA dataset, target-specific fine-tuning of the Boltz-2 affinity head improved potency prediction (Pearson r from 0.248 to 0.560) and reduced mean absolute error. The work aims to make AD target evaluation and modeling reproducible and traceable.

Molecular Dynamics-Guided Triage of Approved Drugs Against Escherichia coli Resistance Targets Nominates Capmatinib, Metergoline and Nilotinib as Candidates for Experimental Testing.

The authors docked 2070 approved drugs against four E. coli antibacterial targets (FabI, LpxC, DHFR, GyrB) and then ran 100 ns triplicate molecular dynamics simulations on top hits plus reference inhibitors. Docking failed to recover known reference inhibitors (e.g., trimethoprim ranked 762nd), highlighting scoring-function biases, but MD-based triage nominated capmatinib, metergoline, and nilotinib as candidates for experimental testing. The work is a methodological cautionary tale about virtual screening reliability combined with a small set of repurposing candidates.
